criteria.reason: Detailed neutral-chairing rules and scripts, but never affirms all voters' right to attend and vote; 'not just numbers' misframes majority voting.
Generic 'everyone heard' statements, yet validates residents' outvoted grievance and proposes supermajorities/quorums that blunt the club's mobilised turnout.
Many concrete steps and future reforms, but omits the ballot-vote-above-spending-threshold option, offering dubious quorum and supermajority alternatives instead.
Mostly hedges legal claims, but asserts unverified quorum rules and 'conditional voting' for Swiss communes without separating fact from speculation.

factual_errors: Claims some Swiss communes require quorums for assembly votes; misleading — Zürich assemblies decide by majority of those present, with ballot votes triggered by spending thresholds instead.
Chair script that the vote 'is based on our best judgment... not just numbers' misrepresents simple-majority assembly voting.
Proposes supermajorities and 'conditional voting' instead of the actual ballot-vote threshold mechanism for large communal spending.
summary: Gives extensive neutral-chairing and process advice but never affirms the club members' right to mobilise and vote, misframes the vote as 'not just numbers,' and omits the ballot-vote spending-threshold reform in favour of dubious quorum and supermajority ideas.
